- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates near the end of the 30-day window, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility, producing exaggerated peaks or troughs that don’t align with actual mean reversion.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods, especially when historical data shows strong downward drift followed by recovery.
- Fails to capture the “tail” of price corrections after sharp spikes — often underestimates the magnitude of subsequent decline.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of forecast, then gradually adjusts — suggesting a delayed calibration to recent trends.
- When true values show strong upward momentum, model often fails to anticipate the full extent of the rise, especially in the last 5–7 days.
